title: AI-generated virtual spatial proteomics reveals lung-cancer tumor–immune niches associated with immunotherapy response
summary: HEX, a pathology-image AI model, predicts spatial expression of 40 protein biomarkers from routine H&E slides. In retrospective NSCLC cohorts, combining HEX-derived virtual spatial proteomics with histology improved prognosis prediction and, in a separate 148-patient immune-checkpoint-inhibitor cohort, improved response prediction over H&E-only and virtual-proteomics-only models. The authors interpreted virtual maps as showing co-localized T-helper and cytotoxic T-cell niches among responders and immunosuppressive macrophage/neutrophil aggregates among non-responders.
ai_technology: HEX (H&E to protein expression), using a pathology foundation-model backbone; MICA (multimodal integration via co-attention)

evidence.tested: In retrospective NSCLC cohorts, combining HEX-derived virtual spatial proteomics with histology improved prognosis prediction and, in a separate 148-patient immune-checkpoint-inhibitor cohort, improved response prediction over H&E-only and virtual-proteomics-only models.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective observational cohorts; predictive associations do not establish causal mechanisms or improved patient outcomes from model-guided treatment. The 148-patient immunotherapy cohort is separate from the prognosis cohorts. The paper itself says extensive clinical validation remains necessary; do not describe the finding as a clinically validated diagnostic or prospective treatment-selection tool.
evidence.ai_role: HEX predicts expression of 40 proteins and produces spatially resolved virtual proteomics from H&E images; MICA fuses the original image with AI-derived maps for outcome prediction. Researchers used predicted marker distributions to interpret therapy-associated tumor–immune spatial patterns. These are retrospective model analyses with cohort-based clinical associations, not prospective treatment evidence.
